_about: Elsewhere Annex v2 (ET · Gremlin Desks only). The world is procedural: a seeded grid of cells. Each section has a crystal plaza at its 'center' cell; every other cell belongs to the nearest section and gets hallways (always safe) plus rooms off them (where grabbers and the rare almost-people live). To add a section: copy a row in 'sections', give it a new id, center [cellX, cellZ] a few cells from the others, palette, crystal and room mix. Cells are grid.cell metres square.
name: The Elsewhere Annex
tagline: The Survey Corps found it. They're still mapping it.

lore.grenshol: Grenshol is a tall black figure who shows up as a soft green flicker. He can't speak, and he can't fully be here, but he plays with newcomers, nudges them toward doors, and pulls people out of trouble. Early on, the Gremlins found a round, warm portal that smelled of rain on ferns. Someone tapped on it and something tapped back, and for years they believed they had let him out. They had it backwards: he came through long before they found it. He's on our side.
lore.firstSighting: A green flicker at the end of the hall, and the smell of warm rain on ferns. That's Grenshol. The notice board says: let him be. He's on our side.

notes.title: Survey page, torn
notes.text: Pulled the stitch from the gallery side. The wall said 'Oh. Finally.' We followed it through and found a clean room already waiting: desks, a board, lamps that work. We're calling it the Door Station. Nobody has checked in yet, but it feels like they will. — Pip

notes.title: Survey page, torn
notes.text: The rooms have started moving. We went back for a bench and the bench was two halls over. Or the halls had moved and the bench hadn't. Hard to say. Chalked the first mark tonight: STAYS PUT ✓. If it holds till morning I'll chalk another. — Pip

notes.title: Survey page, torn
notes.text: A door nobody had noticed turned on its own this morning. Just turned, as if it had been waiting. We stood there a while and decided not to guess. If you find this page, you're already closer than we were. — Pip

notes.title: Survey page, torn
notes.text: We've got it, I think. The hum goes warmer near the places we've marked. They barely change. We're calling them stable places, which the people who live here thought was very funny, because they've had a word for that for years. Also: a green flicker in the corner waved, maybe? Hard to say. We waved back, just in case. — Pip

notes.title: Survey page, torn
notes.text: A surveyor lent her Keepsake to a stranger who asked nicely. She stayed where she stood. Her name's still on the board. We haven't found anything to write after it. The log will be shorter after this.

grid._about: cell = size of one generated block (m). hall = corridor width. Chunks within loadRadius cells of you are built; beyond unloadRadius they're thrown away. spokes = corridors forced open out of each crystal plaza. npcMinDepth = almost-people never appear closer than this many cells to the entrance.

creature.name: Grenshol
creature._name: Bryan named him. Change it here and it changes everywhere. Pronoun: he/him (canon).
creature.about: A tall black figure from somewhere else, seen as a soft green flicker. Never evil, never hurts anyone. He plays, watches, helps and nudges. Catching or tagging him means he carries you to an instance door you haven't found. He never goes inside instances.
creature._where: Only in deeper sections: never in excludeSections (the start), and never closer than minDepth cells to the entrance.

appear: A soft green flicker at the far end of the hall. Something very tall is standing very still.
The air smells faintly of warm rain on ferns. Grenshol is near.
Two quiet taps on the wall beside you. Then a green flicker, down the hall.
freeze: Grenshol goes perfectly still, as if that makes him invisible. Quick, tag him!
He stops mid-step and holds it. He's waiting to see what you'll do.
He freezes. The green flicker steadies for a moment.
flee: …and he folds into a doorway that wasn't there. Gone, for now.
A flicker, a rush of warm air, and he's gone.
He steps back into nothing. The fern smell lingers.
blink: He's behind you now. He wants to play.
Warm, damp air on the back of your neck. Grenshol moved.

creature.caught: Grenshol catches you. Long, careful fingers, a green flicker, and the halls fold away…
creature.tagged: You tag Grenshol! He goes still, then bows, very slightly, and the halls fold away…

carry._about: v6 (lore fact 28): catch or tag = he carries you and sets you down OUTSIDE an instance door you haven't found yet; that door then lights up on the Station facade. He never goes in. If you've found every door he knows, he sets you down at the nearest stable place you've found.

doors.name: the padlocked gate in the Annex That Turns

carry.setDown: …warm, wet air, a last green flicker, and you're standing outside {door}. He's already gone. He never goes in.
carry.allFound: …he sets you down somewhere that stays put: {place}. Every door he knows, you've already found.
carry.stationLit: 🚪 Back at the Door Station, a door just lit up for you: {door}.
carry.fernFrond: There's a fern frond in your pocket that wasn't there before. Nothing in the Annex grows ferns.

teaser._about: v6: the sensory teaser that replaces the full dinosaur-world tour (lore fact 32). Shown during the carry.
lines: A green flicker. For half a heartbeat: tall ferns, warm rain, and the smell of wet earth from somewhere very old. Then it's gone.
Warm rain on ferns. Something huge breathing slowly, somewhere below. Then the halls again.
Green light, wet leaves against your face, a deep call from very far off. Then nothing.

help._about: v6 intensity roles: watching, helping, nudging, rare glimpse.
help.healText: A green flicker brushes past you. Warm rain, the smell of ferns, and your bruises ease (+{hp} HP).
help.pointText: Little stones, stacked into an arrow on the floor, pointing {dir}. Grenshol's work.
help.nudgeText: A green flicker at the edge of your sight, and a long hand on your shoulder, steering you…
watchText: A green flicker, watching from the end of the hall. He doesn't come closer.
Two taps on the wall. He's keeping an eye on you.

minions.name: lampwings
minions.about: Small moth-like lampwings that drift after Grenshol. Sometimes one settles on an almost-person and talks through them for a little while.
possessed: A lampwing settles on an almost-person's head. Their eyes go a soft, bright green.
Something small and fluttering lands on an almost-person's shoulder. They straighten up and turn towards you.
lines: We followed the green. Did you see the green?
Hello, {nameOff}. He says hello. He can't say it himself.
Warm rain. Ferns. Do you know ferns?
He holds what he can. We keep him company.
You walk like someone looking for a door.
release: They blink. "Sorry. What was I saying? Was I saying?"
Their eyes go back to normal. A lampwing drifts off towards the ceiling.
They shake their head, as if to clear it, and wander back to their room.
minions.talkIntro: Their eyes are glowing green. Something small and fluttering is doing the talking.

aliveMode.prompt: See what happens when the lights change?
aliveMode.switchTitle: A light switch that wasn't here before
aliveMode.switchLabel: A light switch that wasn't here before
aliveMode.small: Nothing bad happens. Things just get… livelier for a while.
aliveMode.on: Click. The lights go a strange blue. The chairs shuffle. Somewhere, something tall perks up.
aliveMode.off: The lights settle back to yellow. Everything pretends nothing happened.
aliveMode.decline: You leave it. The switch looks a little disappointed.

stairwells._about: Rooms in a section roll stairChance (per section row) for a stairwell. Kinds: up/down land you in another cell (or, otherSectionChance of the time, another section); loop puts you back at the bottom of the same stairs; flip lands you on an upside-down landing for a few seconds.

messages: You climb fourteen steps up and come out… on the same floor? Somewhere else, anyway: {section}.
Up, up, up. The stairs let out somewhere in {section}. Your ears pop politely.
Down the dark stairs, round a corner that shouldn't fit, and out into {section}.
You go down. And down. And come out on a floor that is definitely higher than where you started. {section}.
You climb up. You arrive at the bottom of the same stairs.
Up the stairs… and you're standing at the foot of them again. The poster looks smug.
You go up. The stairs go round. You are, once again, at the start of the stairs.
You come out on a landing that's upside down. The ceiling is the floor now. ({section}) Give it a moment.
Down the stairs and… everything's upside down. Your coffee isn't. ({section})

stairwells.loopNote: A gremlin note on the banister: "we went round 41 times. it's very good exercise."
stairwells._about_v5d2: v5d2: stairwells are real now. Each kind uses a flight from stairs[] (matched by kind): from/to = floor heights in metres (to > from goes up, below 0 goes down into a pit), steps = number of steps, direction = 'away-from-door' (the only one built), landing = flat landing length, width = flight width. You walk the actual steps (smooth height following, rails on the sides); reaching the landing does the old Escher trick for that kind. gravity 'inverted' is a stub for future upside-down stairs that disorient the room: rows with it are ignored for now (not built).

stairs._note: STUB, not built: upside-down stairs that flip the room around you. Kept here so the shape is settled.

tvs._about: Rooms of these types roll chance for a little TV. Each plays one procedural cartoon (picked by the room's hash) at fps frames per second, and only while it's on screen and within range metres.

_cartoons.sunclock: a smiling sun clocking in at 9:00, again
_cartoons.queue: a queue where the front person goes to the back

glimpse.briefReturn: …and the halls come back, exactly where you were. Your sleeves are damp.

escalation._about: v6c (continuity 105): brief glimpses escalate by how many the player has already seen (saved as prog.glimpse.briefs). Early: ferns, warm rain, a green flicker. After several (3+): add something huge breathing. Late (6+): a deep call from far off. Nothing is ever seen clearly. The full reveal stays behind fullReveal (off).
escalation.early: For a moment you see through a green haze: ferns, warm rain, and a green flicker, somewhere very old…
escalation.mid: Ferns, warm rain, a green flicker. Somewhere out of sight, something huge is breathing. Nothing is clear.
escalation.late: Ferns and warm rain in a green flicker. From very far off, a deep call. Nothing is clear.

beyond._about: v5d2: the open open halls are calm exploring (no wandering critters, no Grenshol, no flitters, no light-switch rooms). Weird doors out in the open halls open onto short passages that are sealed off from the normal halls. Only inside those passages do small random critters and Grenshol show up. Grenshol is from another world: never in the instances (Mailroom, Grotto, Training Closet, gates). Zones are cell rectangles (origin [i,j], size [w,d]); every edge leaving a zone is sealed, every edge inside is open. A door sits flush on a closed wall of its cell (wall is picked automatically; 'wall' is the fallback that gets sealed if every arm is open). Change names/lines freely.

beyond._about_rooms: zones[].rooms marks side rooms inside a zone (cell relative to the zone origin; qi optional). danger:true = a push room: steady, perfect light, a warning plate, and traps. v6 traps: type 'snare' knocks you out (never death, no XP or gear lost) and Grenshol's hand grabs your collar and returns you to the Door Station.

_grabbersAbout: v6: grabbers are Reachers (lore). Type ids stay hem/courtesy/bounceback so saved data and section rows don't change; only the names, lines and the 3D model changed. They tug you to another section of the open halls, never to an instance.

stable._about: v6 stable places (lore 72-75): places that barely change. The shifter never re-rolls them (rooms use epoch 0 and no sliding walls). Marked by warm, gently flickering lamps, a STAYS PUT ✓ chalk mark, the settled 'stable' music scene and the waystone's ring. Each one you find is saved per player and drawn on your map (the rest stays fog). Knockouts in the open halls and the Home crystal go to the nearest one you've found. Plazas (every section's waystone center) count automatically. v6c: map count is '{n} found', never 'of N', because the world keeps growing. Stable lamps flicker warm, slow and even (style warm-even); this is a different motion from intensity's harsh, fast, irregular flicker.
stable.found: 📍 A stable place: {name}. It stays put. It's on your map now.
stable.restText: You sit a while. The fog at the edge of your sight clears, and you get your breath back.
stable.mapTitle: 🗺 Your map: places that stay put
stable.mapNote: Only stable places you've found are drawn. Everything between them is fog: no use drawing a hall that won't be there tomorrow.

intensity._about: v6 intensity (Bryan, Nov 15): some areas and moments ramp up. 0 = calm, 1 = as tense as it gets. Rises in zones past weird doors, push rooms, sections with a base value, and the longer you wander lost; falls in stable places and at the Station. As it climbs: harsh irregular light flicker (not the warm gentle flicker of stable places), the music drops to a dreary variant, and Grenshol appears and watches more often. All tunable here. v6c: intensity flicker is harsh, fast and irregular, and never applies to stable-place lamps or while you are in a stable place. Contrast with stable.lamp.style = warm-even.

grenshol._about: openHalls: he may watch (never chase or catch) in the open halls once intensity >= watchFrom. In zones past weird doors he plays as before. appearEvery = [[minIntensity, [minSec, maxSec]], ...]. On a watch appearance: helpChance (a small heal if HP < helpHpBelow, else stones stacked into an arrow toward the nearest stable place you haven't found), nudge when you've been lost stuckSeconds, rare brief glimpse (glimpseChance, only above glimpseFrom, then a cooldown).

targets._about: What intensity drifts toward. In a zone past a weird door: the zone's own 'intensity' (or zoneDefault); in a push room: pushRoom. In the open halls: sectionBase + being lost a long time (up to lostMax) + moments (a shift about to happen, low HP). Stable places and the Station: 0.

campaign._about: v6c campaign track. Data-driven: chapters → beats. Each beat has a hint, a guide target (warming hum + a lamp one room ahead), a goal, optional breadcrumb logbook pages and a short reflective line. Beat rooms are hand-placed and never re-roll. Progress is per player (prog.campaign). The Survey waypoint is Tallow Camp (continuity 106). Chapter 2 is a data-only stub (playable: false) until Bryan writes the Overlook riddle. Finishers are stored per device; a shared record needs a server.

chapters.outro: Chapter 1 complete. The first survey ends where it began: with a door nobody had noticed.

beats.title: Sign the log
beats.hint: Read the Common Record on the Station's east wall.
beats.reflect: Every name on the board was new here once.

beats.title: A torn page
beats.hint: A logbook page is lying in a room east of the Station. Follow the lamp.
beats.reflect: Pip's handwriting, from the first day. The ink hasn't faded at all.

beats.title: Somewhere that stays put
beats.hint: West of the Station, a bench never moves. Find it and sit a while.
beats.reflect: The halls shift around you. The bench doesn't. You breathe out.

beats.title: Tallow Camp
beats.hint: The Corps keep Tallow Camp south of the bench. Read their chart.
beats.reflect: Someone left a candle stub burning. The same hallway, drawn three times, crossed out. Follow the hum.

beats.title: The door that turns
beats.hint: The chart points east, into the halls that turn. A page marks the way to a door at their edge.

reveal.title: A door where there wasn't one
reveal.text: Back at the Station, a lamp comes on above its twin.

beats.reflect: You found it the way they did: by listening.

beatRooms.label: Tallow Camp
beatRooms.signSub: leave a stub · kept lit by everyone and no one
beatRooms.title: 📜 The survey chart
beatRooms.text: A hand-drawn chart pinned to a field table, ringed with lit candle stubs. Halls drawn, rubbed out, drawn again. One arrow, inked over many times, points east toward the halls that turn. In the margin: “The hum gets warmer when you're close. Trust it. — P.” By Corps custom every surveyor who passes leaves a stub, so the camp is kept lit by everyone and no one.
beatRooms.early: A chart of hallways, most of them crossed out, and a few candle stubs still burning. You'll understand it better later.
beatRooms._about: Tallow Camp (continuity 106). The old 'Survey waypoint' name is retired in player-facing text.
